activeRecallQuiz.scenario: A stock breaks out to a new 52-week high with heavy daily volume, but its Futures Open Interest drops by 15%. Is this a robust, sustainable bull breakout?
activeRecallQuiz.question: A stock breaks out to a new 52-week high with heavy daily volume, but its Futures Open Interest drops by 15%. Is this a robust, sustainable bull breakout?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: No. When price rises while Open Interest declines, traders are liquidating existing contracts. The volume spike represents short-covering panics rather than sustained fresh capital accumulation.
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Applying grounded principles prevents catastrophic losses and capital depletion.

coreTakeaways: Always evaluate underlying market assumptions before entering positions.
Separate gross theoretical payoff from real-world net profit.
Follow disciplined risk and position sizing limits on every trade.
